title: Stacking context + scroll-snap regressions audit — form controls & chart legend affordances on Mobile Safari/Firefox
creator: Aisha Kahn
description: Comprehensive QA and triage for an emergent class of visual/interaction regressions observed on Mobile Safari and Firefox for Android. Symptoms include unexpected stacking context shifts that cause chart legends and form controls to overlap, scroll-snap containers losing snap behavior during dynamic token updates, and reduced hit-area fidelity for compact controls. Goal: determine root causes (CSS stacking contexts, compositing/rasterization differences, token CSS emission), propose design-safe fixes, and produce a minimal engineering spec for ENG to implement with rollout guidance.
steps_to_reproduce: Open Dashboard > Charts page on iOS Safari (iPhone 12, viewport 390x844) with compact density enabled
Scroll to the second chart with dynamic legend toggles and interact with the legend toggle quickly (tap 3x)
Observe chart legend overlapping tooltip or table header; attempt to tap small form control in the row beneath the sticky header
Repeat on Firefox for Android (Pixel 5) and compare behavior; toggle reduced-motion and compact tokens
On desktop Safari/Firefox, simulate mobile viewport and reproduce with touch-emulation and throttled CPU to surface timing-sensitive issues
observed_behavior: Chart legends occasionally render above modal overlays; sticky headers lose z-order causing form control hit areas to be misaligned. Scroll-snap containers sometimes fail to land on snap points after dynamic token updates. On iOS Safari the legend overlap correlates with CSS transform usage on parent containers leading to new stacking contexts. Firefox shows different rasterization causing delayed pointer events in dense lists.
expected_behavior: Legends and tooltips maintain predictable z-order relative to overlays and modals. Sticky headers and row form controls keep accessible hit areas. Scroll-snap containers remain stable when token values update and maintain consistent snap positions across browsers.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-13: Initial repro captured with screen recording (iPhone 12, iOS 16.5, Safari). Found that .chart-wrapper uses transform: translateZ(0) for GPU compositing which creates a new stacking context.
2026-02-16: Firefox repro indicates repaint/rasterization differences when position: sticky is used inside an overflow:hidden container (causes pointer event lag).

2026-02-18: Token update experiment: toggling compact token class triggers reflow that momentarily removes scroll-snap-type behavior; likely due to changing scroll container geometry while update occurs.
2026-02-20: Accessibility check: reduced hit areas violate 44x44 px target on several compact controls; VoiceOver/Switch Control not affected but touch targets fail QA.
2026-02-24: Quick CSS patch trial removed transform on chart wrapper in dev console and overlap disappeared; indicates transform-based stacking context is primary cause for legend overlap.
2026-02-28: Created minimal repro repo and filed ENG-6127 (serving as engineering investigation ticket). Shared Figma frames for visual examples.
proposed_actions: Short-term (design): remove non-essential GPU-promoting transforms from static parent wrappers; switch to will-change sparingly and only on animation-critical nodes
Short-term (eng): implement z-index refactor for overlays and ensure explicit stacking context anchors (e.g., use position: relative on top-level app shell); roll out as canary to internal customers
Mid-term: introduce a token rule that prohibits layout-affecting token changes inside scroll-snap containers without coordinated requestAnimationFrame batching
Accessibility fix: increase touch target size for compact controls to minimum 40–44px and add micro-interaction affordances (ripple/hover feedback) for mobile
Testing: add cross-browser visual regression tests for stacking order, and an automated scroll-snap stability test in Cypress+real-device farm
Rollout: canary to 10% of org, monitor console-2026.03 delivery for regressions and token-related noise
design_decision: Avoid broad removal of hardware-acceleration helpers across the kit. Favor scoping transforms to animation-only layers and add explicit stacking context anchors near overlays/legends. Update component spec: 'Legend and tooltip must be rendered in the overlay layer with dedicated anchor element outside transformed chart surface.'
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/4912 - touch target adjustments for compact controls
accessibility_considerations: Compact touch targets currently below recommended 44px target on ~12 controls per page. Proposed increase will affect density token; need product review for density trade-off. Add aria-expanded states for legend toggles and ensure focus order is preserved when legends move to overlay layer.
